title: Harness of Minervini v2 ticker.risk response

examples: scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline ticker risk AAPL --market-state favorable --eligibility-state eligible --setup-state ready --fundamentals-state supports_convergence --entry-price 200 --stop-price 188 --upside-price 224 --average-gain-pct 24
scripts/.venv/bin/python scripts/pipeline ticker risk AAPL --mode active --entry-price 200 --entry-date 2026-08-10 --stop-price 188

exit_codes.0: A valid domain envelope was emitted; its status may still be partial, unavailable, or needs_input.
exit_codes.2: The request or arguments were invalid; stdout contains a needs_input error envelope.
exit_codes.3: An unexpected internal contract failure occurred; stdout contains an unavailable error envelope.

as_of.description: Completed US trading session in YYYY-MM-DD form; defaults to the latest completed regular session.

average_gain_pct.description: The trader's realized average gain percentage. Prospective mode cannot reach BUY-READY without it; its absence is reported as missing evidence, not a relaxed cap. In active mode it is one of the two reference points for selling into strength, reported as a distance from the position's return and never as a trigger.

base_count.description: How many bases this stage 2 advance has formed, counted by the analyst. It is reported against the three-to-five range the source names for a typical top, together with the source's own disclaimer that base counting cannot say a stock has topped. It never becomes an action.

base_top.description: The top of the base the position broke out from. With it, the last close's extension over the base top is reported against the 20-25 pause zone TraderLion describes, and sitting inside that zone is a tagged REVIEW action; past it or short of it is evidence only.

breakout_date.description: The session of the breakout. It anchors the since-breakout windows: the key-reversal criteria, the gap-up count and the latest gap's fate, and the breakout session's volume ratio against the fifty sessions before it -- a later down session heavier than the breakout session is the sell-or-reduce REVIEW Minervini describes. Every one of them is doctrine about what a stock does after it breaks out, so without this date they are reported unavailable under breakout_date_not_declared rather than measured from the entry session -- an early or cheat entry has not broken out yet, and reading post-breakout behavior into it would answer a question the doctrine never asked. The same withholding applies to the pause-zone review that --base-top raises.

completed_stop_breach.description: Assert a stop breach on completed evidence.

current_price.description: Optional explicit latest completed price. A value at or below the stop can trigger SELL, but a value above it cannot establish HOLD without the provider-audited completed price path.

earnings_date.description: The next earnings report for this position. A report still ahead of --as-of is a REVIEW action: Minervini tells a holder to be aware of the coming report and of the same industry group's, and the harness reports beside it that Zanger, a practitioner it reads for contrast, has not held through a release in more than ten years. A report already behind the position is evidence only. Left out, an active request about the current session looks it up: an unstated date is a gap in what the analyst typed, not in what is knowable. A request naming an explicit --as-of declines the lookup instead, because a calendar entry is a forecast and no feed can say what it forecast on a past session. The block names where the date came from and whether the feed confirmed it or answered with a window it guessed at, and the earlier edge of a window is the one published -- a holder asking whether a report is still ahead needs the first session it could land on.

eligibility_state.description: The eligibility the caller settled themselves. avoid and incomplete stand; eligible leaves the plane unattested. Attach the ticker.qualify envelope under --evidence for an eligibility that counts.

entry_date.description: Actual ISO entry date; required in active mode.

entry_price.description: Positive planned or actual entry price.

evidence.description: The component envelopes this verdict is reduced from -- market.snapshot, ticker.qualify, ticker.setup, ticker.fundamentals -- each whole, as the capability returned it. This is the only channel through which a component plane passes. Four checks run before one counts, and each is something this capability can settle without re-measuring: the attachment is a v2 envelope rather than a dict carrying the fields read here, it is about this ticker and this session, its sources list is not empty because an envelope that reached no provider measured nothing, and no other attachment already settles the same plane -- two both claiming one plane are refused rather than ranked, since keeping the last hands the verdict to argument order. Status ok and partial both count: a market read is favorable with context evidence missing, and fundamentals support convergence without every optional figure. The plane's word is then read from the envelope's own payload rather than from anything declared beside it. A refused envelope leaves its plane unattested and names the check it failed. The state flags below remain the way to declare a plane the caller settled themselves, and they can only make the verdict more cautious -- a declared failure or wait still binds over an attached envelope that passes, because a person who read this stock is not overruled by a capability that did not. BUY-READY is reached from envelopes or not at all.

format.description: Output detail only; compact preserves verdict, signals, and missing evidence while omitting verbose basis rows.

fundamentals_state.description: The fundamentals the caller settled themselves. does_not_support_convergence and incomplete stand; supports_convergence leaves the plane unattested. Attach the ticker.fundamentals envelope under --evidence for fundamentals that count.

initial_stop_price.description: The hard stop the trade started with, for when --stop-price has since been raised. Initial risk is entry minus this, and R multiples and 3R protection are measured from it; without it a raised stop leaves R unmeasured rather than measured from the wrong risk. Declaring it beside a different --stop-price requires --stop-effective-date, because a raised stop was raised on some date.

invalidation_condition.description: Observable structural invalidation condition. Pair it with --invalidation-price in active mode: the level is audited on completed closes, which is what a structural condition is about, and a condition the harness cannot evaluate against completed bars is reported as missing evidence rather than assumed unbreached.

invalidation_price.description: Positive structural invalidation price. In active mode it is audited over completed closes from --entry-date, alongside and independently of the hard stop, which is audited over Lows.

live_stop_breach.description: Assert a live breach; SELL requires live_stop_check too.

management_average.description: The moving average the trader manages the position by, declared as their own exit plan: ema21 for swing management, sma50 for a position trail (the TraderLion role split). Two completed closes below it, both inside the position, are audited over completed bars like a stop and are a SELL. Both averages are measured either way; the one not declared reports two closes below it as a REVIEW action.

management_profile.description: Opt into a tagged TraderLion practice-layer management default. tl_stage12 is the Stage 1 and 2 rule: once the position has shown a 5 percent profit, REDUCE half and RAISE_STOP to breakeven. A profile adds management_actions under HOLD, each marked binds false and source [TL], and never touches the verdict.

market_state.description: The market read the caller settled themselves. It can withhold BUY-READY and can never produce it -- a favorable word here leaves the plane unattested, because the word is free to type and this reducer cannot check it. Attach the market.snapshot envelope under --evidence for a market that counts. In active mode this is the market defense input, where it tightens stops and touches no verdict.

no_cache.description: Bypass both provider-cache reads and writes for this invocation.

setup_state.description: The setup the caller settled themselves. wait, avoid and incomplete stand; ready leaves the plane unattested. Attach the ticker.setup envelope under --evidence for a setup that counts.

stage2_start.description: The session the stage 2 advance began. With it, the largest daily and weekly decline since then are measured and the latest completed session or week being that decline is a REVIEW action that needs the chart; without it that block is reported unavailable rather than measured from an arbitrary start.

stop_effective_date.description: Calendar date when --stop-price became effective in active mode; defaults to --entry-date. The audit begins with the first completed bar on or after this date.

stop_price.description: Positive hard-stop price. In active mode, every completed daily Low is audited from the stop's effective date through --as-of.

upside_price.description: Positive evidence-based reward reference; required in prospective mode.

limitations: This capability never recommends portfolio allocation or position size. A REDUCE action names a fraction of the position, which is a selling discipline, not an allocation.
A hard stop may not exceed 10% or half the realized average gain; --average-gain-pct is required for a prospective verdict and reward-to-risk must be at least 2:1.

A completed current price above the protective level cannot establish HOLD: the provider must cover every completed daily Low from --stop-effective-date through --as-of; a recovered price does not erase an earlier breach.

Each protective level is audited from its own effective date, and against the price its own kind of level is a level of. The hard stop runs from --stop-effective-date against every completed daily Low, because a stop is an order resting in the market and the tape takes it out intraday. The structural invalidation runs from --entry-date against every completed close, because it is a statement about where a session finished -- the condition a caller writes beside one says "completed close below", and a poke through the level that closed back above it is not the exit they declared. That difference decides the boundary too: a Low that reached the stop reached the order, while a close that stopped exactly on the invalidation has not gone below it. Each audit names the basis it used. When one session broke both, the record is about the stop -- the Low prints before the close, so the position was already out when the close invalidated, and a completed close handed in below a resting stop proves the session traded at least that low -- and among levels read from the same price it is about the highest. A breach of either is a SELL, and HOLD requires every declared level to be cleared over its whole window -- cleared by an audit of its own kind of price. A window where no Low reached a level is a window no close fell below either, so the order audit answers both questions; the reverse does not hold, and a cleared invalidation read as a cleared stop is how an order the tape took out intraday goes unreported. A session whose own prices contradict each other -- a close under its low, an open above its high, a high beneath its low -- is refused whole, because which of the four numbers is wrong is unknowable and the audit reading Lows and the price read from the Close would otherwise answer one question two ways.
--stop-effective-date defaults to --entry-date. When a stop was raised or replaced later, supply its actual effective date so the newer stop is not applied retroactively.

Active-mode chronology is checked before any evidence is fetched: --entry-date cannot follow --as-of, and --stop-effective-date can neither precede --entry-date nor follow --as-of. A stop in force from the entry session sits below the price the position was entered at, or the trade runs no risk for it to bound; a stop raised later, on its own effective date, is free to defend a gain above entry, and then there is no loss below entry to report, so the difficult-market band is left unmeasured rather than handed a negative distance. An asserted breach outranks evidence nobody gathered, but never a request that contradicts itself or declares no exit plan.

An explicit --current-price at or below the stop can trigger SELL; a partial-session breach must instead use the explicit live-stop flags. That price is dated --as-of, which is the latest date any exit can carry, so it never stands in for the completed-bar audit: the bars are still fetched, and an exit they already printed happened first and names the failure. It reads each level the way that level's own audit reads it, so equality decides the same way on both sides. It fills in only where the audit could not speak, and never where the audit refused because the window spans a corporate action -- there the declared level and the price are in two coordinate systems, and the price is withheld with the window. Where it does decide the record, it is the price published beside it, because one session cannot have two latest prices. When the provider has nothing to give, the price is the whole record and the structural blocks report price_history_unavailable rather than vanishing.
A live stop breach triggers SELL only when --live-stop-check is explicit; ordinary gates use completed bars.

A completed breach records the breaching session's Open and whether it opened below the level (gap_through_stop): a stop the market gapped through was never available at its price, and the record does not pretend it was. A breach also names the level it is about in governing_role: price falls from above, so among the levels one session or one price broke, the record is about the highest -- the line it crossed first -- and only a level whose own window still reaches --as-of can be broken by a price printed today. A breached invalidation and a breached stop are both a SELL and are not the same finding. An explicit --current-price at or below one level says only that: a level below it is reported unaudited rather than clear, since one price cannot say what a session last week did. An asserted breach (--completed-stop-breach, --live-stop-breach) is about the declared stop and needs one: with no --stop-price it asserts nothing, and an invalidation plan cannot stand in for the level. An assertion settles the verdict, not the record: it says the position ended without saying when, so the bars are read anyway and an exit they already printed names the failure. What a settled verdict buys is that those bars going missing cannot downgrade it -- they were consulted, not depended on. It does not outrank bars that were read and say the opposite: an asserted breach beside an audit that cleared every declared level over its whole window is a request contradicting itself, and comes back INCOMPLETE naming that rather than as either half of it. A completed_price_path handed in whole is the exception, being the same record the bars would produce -- but only when it is one, in every coordinate: it names a role this request declared, checks that role's own declared level, was audited against the prices that role's audit reads, reports a price that actually crossed the level, and is dated inside the window the position existed in. A record that misses any of them describes some other position, and settling this request on it skips the audit that would have found this one still open. A state word on its own is an assertion wearing the shape of an audit, and it meets the bars like any other. When two exits both happened, the earliest dated one names the failure -- a stop print weeks after a declared average already closed the position is a level that position could not have reached. Two on one session are ordered by when inside it they happened rather than by which is which: a stop the Low reached and a live breach are the session in progress, while a close below an average and a level read from the close are settled at the bell.

The reducer does not infer unsupported market, eligibility, setup, or fundamentals states, and what the caller declares is read as strictly as the bars are. A declared component must be an object, and its state must be a word from that component's own vocabulary -- the same list the flags accept. An unrecognised word is refused rather than interpreted, because read through a triggered-or-not test it would silently mean untriggered and through a clear-or-breached test it would silently mean unaudited, and either way an input nobody can interpret would decide a verdict by not being understood. Dates are ISO calendar dates written YYYY-MM-DD: the basic form and a bare number parse in one half of the harness and read as absent in the other, which is how one field comes to have two answers. Prices are finite positive numbers, including --current-price and --entry-price, and one small enough to round away at the reported precision is refused too, since every measurement divided by it comes back infinite beside a zero. A number that is not a price is neither dropped nor honoured: dropping --current-price falls back on the provider and answers a question the caller asked a different way, and honouring it sells the position at a price that is not a price.

A down session that traded heavier than the breakout session is reported as that comparison and nothing more. The source's pattern is a low-volume breakout followed by high-volume selling, and neither "low" nor "high" has a boundary anywhere in the corpus, so the action is named after what the bars settled and does not borrow the source's sell-or-reduce guidance for a pattern its own evidence leaves unresolved. Two closes below --management-average sell because the trader declared that average as their exit plan, not because TraderLion's rule binds this harness; the same two closes below the average not declared are a REVIEW action. A declared average the bars cannot read (too little history) leaves HOLD unestablished, like an unaudited stop.

Weeks are read to the Friday. A trailing week with no Friday session is not promoted to completed -- without a trading calendar an exchange holiday and an unfinished week look the same -- but it is published beside the finding as pending_week_ending with its own change, so a week the block declined to weigh is never silently dropped. A close below the 20-day average and the largest decline of the advance are REVIEW evidence, never a SELL on their own: the source calls the first a judgment call and the second a sell signal in most cases, and keeps the hard stop as the only automatic exit.

One stop raise is expressible: --initial-stop-price with --stop-effective-date splits the audit into the level that governed before the raise and the level in force since. A position whose stop moved twice cannot be described here, and the intermediate level is not audited.

A window is only as good as the bars inside it. The audit reports the first and last bar it actually read, including when an unusable price ends it early -- a window read up to the session it stopped being readable in is not a window nothing was read in -- and an --entry-date the provider printed no bar for makes the position unauditable rather than clear -- a stop may be moved on a day the market was shut, but a position cannot be opened on one. Sessions missing in the middle of a window cannot be told from market holidays without a trading calendar, which this harness does not carry.

A structure measurement is unavailable rather than approximated: a frame carrying a NaN or non-positive price, a --breakout-date with no completed bar, a history that begins after the window it is asked about, and a provider frame without Open or Volume each name what is missing instead of publishing a number computed around it. A block built from several measurements is unavailable when every one of them is -- a Stage 3 vector with neither true range and no long-average slope is not a reading with nothing in it.

Prices are the ones the tape printed, unadjusted, with the split events beside them. A share split inside an audit or measurement window puts the declared entry and stop in one coordinate system and the closes in another, so the window is refused from the event onward rather than measured across. The event is stamped on the session that printed the new prices, so a window that opens on that session is entirely inside the new system and is audited normally -- a position opened after a split, with a stop declared in the new prices, never crosses anything -- a breach the audit already found before it stands, because an event two sessions later cannot un-take-out a stop the market took out. Each measurement asks about its own window: a split before the sessions a simple average reads is outside it, while the recursive average runs from the first bar and spans everything. A refusal names the sessions it did read before the event, and a declared exit those sessions already triggered is published as the breach it was. The refusal reports the window unavailable rather than measured across -- including the current price, which would otherwise sell a position the market never took out. A history that carries no split column has not said there was no split, so a close-to-close change of a fifth or more -- the ratio of a five-for-four, the smallest ordinary split -- is refused the same way under corporate_action_evidence_missing: the harness cannot tell a share count changing from a fall the market made, and the two call for opposite answers. The highest High since entry is withheld on the same finding, under max_high_withheld_reason, because three R measured across an event is a gain the position never had. A split column that is present but unreadable -- an empty cell, a value that is not a number -- has not said there was no split either, and is refused as corporate_action_evidence_missing rather than filled in as a zero. The structure blocks read the event boundary exactly as the audit does, so one frame is not two different frames to two readers.

Post-breakout doctrine needs --breakout-date. The 20-day rule the source states begins "Once the stock successfully breaks out" and the pause zone is an extension a stock pauses at after breaking out, so both publish their measurement with the reason the action was withheld beside it. The tennis-ball behavior, the first sessions out of the base, the gaps since the breakout and the key-reversal criteria have nothing to measure without it and are unavailable outright. A declared date the bars cannot find -- no completed session printed on it, or the returned history begins after it -- is not an anchor either, and the actions are withheld under that reason rather than the date being taken on trust.

The favorable excursion is measured from the session after entry: a daily bar cannot say whether its High printed before or after the fill, and crediting the entry session's own spike would raise a stop and cut a position on a gain that never happened. The last completed close remains the floor of what was reached. It is a statistic over every session held, so it is read whole: one unusable High, or a history that begins after --entry-date, withholds the peak under max_high_withheld_reason rather than publishing the highest of the sessions that happened to come back. The extension block's max_extension_pct reads the same window, so how far the position got is one number rather than two.

Market weakness can raise a stop and can never sell a position: the source tightens stops and lets price action take him out one position at a time. The sizing half of the same passage -- reduce exposure with regard to position sizes -- is deliberately not implemented, because this capability never prescribes size. No stop is ever ordered above the last completed close, whether it comes from three-R protection or from the profile's breakeven half: a level price has already come back through is a sale rather than a stop, and the protection that was missed is reported as not placeable instead.

Every block is guarded by the columns and the sessions it actually reads, so a broken bar voids the readings that touch it and no others: a NaN volume last Friday does not void a gap count that reads Opens, and a NaN Low two hundred sessions back does not void a fourteen-session true range. A statistic over a population is stricter, because it opens every member: the volume percentile ranks the latest session against every prior one and the decline ratio averages the fifty sessions before it, so one unreadable session in either produces no number rather than a rank or an average over the bars that happened to be there. A split inside a volume population is the same hole reached from the other side -- the volumes before it count a different share -- and it withholds the statistic without voiding a block whose own window is on this side of the event. Two fields say different things about what a block did not read. missing_inputs names evidence the block wanted and the history did not hold -- a column that is absent, a session whose value is unusable, or a population that cannot be averaged, which is why volume_history and volume_baseline are named apart: the first is a session's own volume, the second the fifty sessions behind it. claim_inputs_not_read names evidence the cited claim lists that this particular reading never consumes, and it is subtracted from the claims themselves rather than kept by hand beside each block, so a citation cannot quietly come to cover less than it says: the climax vector measures price and volume and never the base count, the management trail measures daily averages and never the weekly context its roles claim asks for, the 20-day reading never opens the stop its rule mentions, and the base-count disclaimer is quoted beside a declared count without reading price or volume history. An INCOMPLETE active verdict carries no management_evidence: those measurements are keyed to a position the request never established. A SELL keeps them, because there the position was real and the structure is part of why it ended. A reading that has to stop stops where the trouble starts rather than losing the window: a split and an unreadable close both bound a management-average audit at their own session, and the values before it were computed from readable closes in one coordinate system -- so a declared exit those sessions already triggered is published as the breach it was, and a hole three weeks later cannot take it back.
x-capability-contract.output: The sole final ticker verdict with component states, completed stop-path evidence, failed/waiting/missing evidence, stop constraints, reward-to-risk, and 3R protection context. attested_evidence is one entry per attached envelope naming the plane it settled and the word it carried, plus refused where a check turned it away and yielded_to_declared where a caller's own more cautious word stood over it; unattested names each plane that did not pass and why -- a state word with no envelope behind it, or the check the envelope failed -- because that gap is closed by running a capability rather than by supplying evidence. An active HOLD also carries management_actions -- what to do while holding, each naming its action (RAISE_STOP, REDUCE, or REVIEW), the claim it comes from, and the measurement behind it; the list is empty when nothing is due, and SELL and INCOMPLETE carry no actions because there is nothing left to manage or no established position to manage. Beside them, management_evidence holds the structural measurements the actions were read from -- both management averages with their two-close audit and, at a breach, the quality of the second close (distance from the average, closing range, whether it held above the first close and the first low); the 20-day average against the last close; and, given --stage2-start, the largest daily and weekly decline of the advance with the session's volume ratio -- so a HOLD with an untouched stop and deteriorating structure reads as HOLD plus REVIEW, never as a bare HOLD. Given --base-top and --breakout-date it also measures selling-into-strength context: the extension over the base top against the 20-25 pause zone, the extension from each management average in percent and ATR beside the stock's own history of extensions, the six key-reversal criteria (three computed, three unresolved -- two are chart readings and the sixth asks for a close low in the range the source never bounds), the gap-ups since the breakout and the latest gap's fate, short-horizon returns with the last session's volume rank, and whether a down session since the breakout was heavier than the breakout session itself. These are measurements with their claims beside them; only the pause zone and the heavier-selling event become REVIEW actions, and none of them can sell. Time is evidence too: the block reports the sessions since entry, the sessions since the last new closing high, every natural reaction since the breakout with its depth and how long recovery took, and the first two sessions out of the base that Zanger reads for volume and price -- the tennis-ball reading Minervini describes, measured and left to the analyst. A declared --market-state of cautious or defensive measures the loss from the level actually in force -- a stop is never widened, so an initial stop above a later, looser one is the level every measurement reads -- and raises the stop toward the five-to-six percent loss range the source cuts at in a difficult environment and never sells the ticker on an opinion of the market. Two more blocks carry calendar and base context: an earnings date still ahead of --as-of is a REVIEW carrying the contrast that one practitioner never holds through a release at all -- declared with --earnings-date, or looked up for an active position on a current request and marked as fetched with the feed's own confirmation beside it -- and --base-count is reported against the three-to-five band with the source's own disclaimer that counting bases cannot call a top. A stage 3 vector travels with every active verdict that has a position -- the recent average true range against the earlier one, and the 200-session average's slope -- as measurements a chart reading is meant to finish, never as an action. No stop is ordered without a last completed price to place it against: with none, placeability is reported unavailable rather than assumed, in the market-defense and the breakeven rules alike. Breakeven protection is reported rather than ordered once price has come back through it: a stop above the last completed close is a sale, not a stop, so risk_controls carries breakeven_protection_not_placeable instead of a RAISE_STOP. Three R is measured from the highest completed High after the entry session (max_high_since_entry, with its date), not from the last close: a gain that was reached and given back is exactly what the rule protects, and the last close is only the floor of what was reached when no High is available. Every limit comes from the doctrine registry: a gate decides pass or fail, while a band such as the ordinary loss target reports the measurement, the source's range, where the measurement sat against that range, and which edge of it is the good one -- a stop tighter than the range is outside it on the favourable side.
prerequisites: Prospective mode should consume market.snapshot, ticker.qualify, ticker.setup, and ticker.fundamentals verdicts.

status_meanings.needs_input: Required evidence is missing, so the domain verdict is INCOMPLETE.
status_meanings.ok: A complete BUY-READY, WAIT, AVOID, HOLD, or SELL verdict was produced; active HOLD includes a clear completed stop path.
status_meanings.partial: The completed-price provider failed, could not cover the full active stop window, or stopped before the requested session.
status_meanings.unavailable: An internal required capability cannot be evaluated.

x-capability-contract.summary: Reduce converged prospective evidence to BUY-READY, WAIT, AVOID, or INCOMPLETE, or active-position evidence to HOLD, SELL, or INCOMPLETE.
